memory.content: Find newsletters and marketing emails the user doesn't read across inbox, archive, and trash, and unsubscribe from them only after they confirm the list.

If nearly all bulk mail is marked read and archived, read status doesn't show what the user ignores; pick unsubscribe candidates by sender address and message type (marketing vs notification), and never unsubscribe from notification streams like payment requests.

# Email unsubscribe sweep

Read-only until the user confirms. Never unsubscribe, click, label, or trash before they approve a specific list.

## 1. Scan
- Use the user's email connector (e.g. Gmail). Confirm the account first.
- Look at the last ~90 days across inbox, archive, and trash; exclude spam, sent, and drafts.
- Start with unread mail, but check whether read status means anything: if most bulk mail is already marked read/archived, unread is a weak signal. Switch to a volume-based scan of all bulk mail.

## 2. Group by exact sender address, not brand
Brands often send promos and notifications from different addresses. For each address record: message count, 3 sample subjects, List-Unsubscribe header (mailto / URL), List-Unsubscribe-Post (one-click), or a body/footer unsubscribe link.

## 3. Classify each address
An unsubscribe header only means the mail is automated. Decide by what triggered it, judged across all of that address's subjects:
- Marketing/newsletter: sent on the sender's schedule to a list (offers, newsletters, digests, event marketing, product updates, surveys); generic subjects, steady cadence.
- Notification/transactional (exclude even with an unsubscribe header): triggered by the user's activity or account (payment requests and receipts, statements, orders/shipping/returns, security and 2FA, alerts the user set up like price alerts or saved searches, real people, calendar, dev/work account alerts, building/package notices, bills); subjects name the user, an amount, an order, or an account event.
- Mixed: the same address sends both. Don't unsubscribe; suggest turning off marketing in that service's settings.
- Also exclude any sender the user has replied to, starred, or filed under a user label.

## 4. Present for confirmation
- Summarize: marketing senders by volume, mixed senders, and a short list of excluded notification senders so the user trusts the split.
- Then send a multi-step checkbox card (multiSelect steps, max 8 steps x 6 options). Card title: "Ticked senders will NOT be unsubscribed. I'll unsubscribe you from everything left unticked." Each step prompt: "<Group>: select ones to KEEP receiving emails from". Give top senders their own box with 90-day counts; group small senders by type (travel, jobs, surveys, apartment, shopping, misc) to fit.
- Unticked = unsubscribe. Confirm the keep list back in one line before starting.

## 5. Unsubscribe (only confirmed senders)
- One-click (RFC 8058): POST List-Unsubscribe=One-Click (form-encoded) to the https header URL; 2xx/3xx counts as accepted. Usually most senders.
- URL / body link: GET it; if the page confirms, done; if it needs a button, form, bot check, or sign-in, mark 'needs browser' and keep the URL.
- mailto only: an outgoing email under the user's name, so never send it unasked; offer to draft it.
- No link at all (some banks, airlines, Apple, rewards programs): needs the user signed in to that account's email settings.
- Report: count done, then the leftovers grouped as opt-out pages I can finish in the browser, sign-in needed, email needed, and failed links. Note mail may trickle in for 1-2 weeks. Ask whether to handle the rest; offer a periodic re-sweep routine.

# Getting started

I find the newsletters and marketing emails you ignore and unsubscribe you from them, but only after you confirm the list, and I never touch notifications like payment requests, receipts, or security alerts.

Ask one at a time:
1. Which email account should I clean up? If Gmail (or their provider's connector) isn't connected, offer it and show the connect card.
2. How hands-on do you want to be: review every list before I unsubscribe (default), or let me handle obvious junk and check only on unclear ones?
3. Any senders or kinds of mail you always want to keep (e.g. newsletters you subscribed to on purpose)?
4. Want me to re-sweep on a schedule (e.g. monthly) for new senders?

Then save their answers as memories, create the routine if they asked for one, and run the email-unsubscribe-sweep skill right away.
